description: A camera for the iOS Simulator: your app's AVFoundation, VisionCamera, expo-camera or Flutter camera code runs unmodified
rules: Run `npx stuntcam up` before launching the app in the iOS Simulator; the app needs no code, dependency or project changes.

Requires an Apple silicon Mac and Xcode 27. iOS Simulator runtimes 17.5, 26.3, 27.0 and 27.2 are verified; on others, `stuntcam up` runs a self-test first and won't arm a simulator where the camera doesn't work.
Xcode Run (⌘R) and Xcode tests need boot mode: run `npx stuntcam up` with the simulator shut down (`--udid <simulator>` boots it armed), or `npx stuntcam up --reboot` if it is already booted.
React Native / Expo: `npx stuntcam up`, then `npx expo run:ios`. Flutter: `npx stuntcam up`, then `flutter run`.

UI tests and CI: `npx stuntcam up --udid $SIM --grant <bundle id>` grants camera and microphone; then `npx stuntcam exec -- xcodebuild test -scheme <scheme> -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIM"`. Use `id=` destinations, not `name=`.

Show your own picture with `npx stuntcam source image:/path/photo.png` or `video:/path/clip.mov`, or your Mac's camera with `npx stuntcam source webcam`; `npx stuntcam source scene` returns to the built-in test scene.
Show a QR code of any text with `npx stuntcam source qr:'https://example.com/pay?id=42'` (quote the text for the shell; up to 2331 bytes).
If the camera doesn't appear, run `npx stuntcam doctor`. `npx stuntcam down` turns stuntcam off without a reboot.
VisionCamera 4 compiles its camera code out of simulator builds and can't work; use VisionCamera 5.
